Transition counts used as predictive features resemble target encoding: including the supervised transition lets its label increase its own feature. Leave-one-user-out estimation uses C₋ᵤ(a,b)=C(a,b)−Cᵤ(a,b), excluding the user’s entire contribution, including repeated occurrences; recompute normalization and support gates consistently. User-level cross-fitting instead builds counts outside each user fold and transforms that fold. All windows from one user must stay together. These principles follow [cross-fitting documentation](https://sklearn.org/stable/auto_examples/preprocessing/plot_target_encoder_cross_val.html) and [grouped splitting](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.GroupKFold.html). Implementation requires stable user IDs or preassigned fold provenance; padded/truncated sequences cannot reliably identify users. A loader returning None needs upstream provenance or precomputed features.

Critical implication: an edge supported by only one user disappears for that user’s training examples, yet becomes available when inference uses full training counts. Cross-fitting prevents self-inclusion; it does not eliminate this support mismatch. Smoothing cannot manufacture independent singleton evidence. Possible controls: consistent minimum distinct-user support, shrinkage toward a prior, and validation of full-count versus fold-count inference. A stronger alignment strategy trains each scorer on users excluded from a fixed reference-count partition, then uses that same table at inference; ensemble partitions if affordable. These are methodological deductions, consistent with [CatBoost’s analysis of prediction shift](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.09516).

For latest items (a,b,c), summing adjacent-count scores C(a,j), C(b,j), C(c,j) combines first-order evidence with recency weights; it is not a third-order model. Distance-matched evidence instead uses lag-three C₃(a,j), lag-two C₂(b,j), and lag-one C₁(c,j). Windowed skip-counts and matrix powers are different estimators; specify collection distances, direction, weighting, smoothing, and identical training/inference semantics. [Sequential transition probes](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) explicitly distinguish pairwise aggregation from joint contextual modeling.
